text: Risk management is the process of identifying possible problems before they happen. First, you need to find out what risks exist, such as financial losses, accidents, or delays. After identifying risks, you should develop mitigation strategies to reduce their impact. For example, you can buy insurance or train staff properly. It is also wise to prepare contingency plans, which are backup plans you can use if something goes wrong. Finally, monitoring is essential because risks change over time. By checking your situation regularly, you can spot new dangers early and adjust your plans. Good risk management helps people and businesses feel safer and more prepared for the future.
